transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-22
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Sable CTO), Ethan Ruiz (Sable ML Eng), Priya Kapoor (Sable Infra)

Summary (auto):
Quick discovery to understand Sable's latency SLOs (p95), concurrency and streaming needs. Discussed tradeoffs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private, KV cache reuse, quantization, and fallbacks. Action items and benchmarks agreed.

[00:00:00] Laura (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. Quick intros?
[00:00:08] Maya (Sable): Yeah, Maya here, CTO at Sable, we run a conversational inference layer for our customer analytics product.
[00:00:12] Ethan (Sable): Ethan, ML infra, I'll be doing the bench work on our side.
[00:00:15] Priya (Sable): Priya, infra lead, network and security questions mostly.
[00:00:20] Laura: Awesome. Samir from Redwood is our SE, he does the deep perf and bench stuff. Samir, you wanna say hi?
[00:00:26] Samir (Redwood SE): Hey, hi all. We'll talk p95s, streaming, token/sec, and hopefully a plan to run a small pilot.

[00:01:10] Maya: To be blunt, our SLAs are tight. For short responses (User -> single-turn answers, 30-80 tokens) we target p95 < 250ms. For streaming long responses (500-1,000 tokens) p95 should be under 1.2s for first token and good steady tail throughput. We get big spikes during end-of-month analytics runs.
[00:01:40] Ethan: Concurrency-wise, steady-state is about 120 concurrent sessions, but bursts hit 800-1,200 for 10-20 minutes.
[00:01:50] Priya: We also have strict data residency and SOC 2 requirements. Private or VPC option is preferred if it simplifies audits.

[00:02:30] Samir: Ok, thanks. Quick validation — are those p95 numbers end-to-end from user to token emitted, including network? Or app-to-model?
[00:02:42] Maya: End-to-end, yes. Example: web socket to backend to model and back. So edges and routing matter.
[00:02:50] Samir: Got it. We typically separate network hop SLOs from model inference p95, but for sizing we will bench end-to-end and model-only. For short responses on our Hosted API we've seen p95 around 120-220ms for 8k context models on good routes; streaming first-token often 400-700ms depending on model variant and quantization.
[00:03:15] Ethan: Those numbers sound promising. Is that with caching or without?
[00:03:20] Samir: Mixed. We do continuous batching and prefix/KV caching; the high-performing numbers assume cache hits for a fair share of requests. Cold KV cache runs will be slower — could double latency depending on model size and hw.

[00:04:05] Priya: For Private, what's the deployment footprint? How many GPUs and what hardware do you recommend?
[00:04:12] Samir: For your burst profile, we'd recommend a Dedicated pool equivalent to roughly 3-4 A100-class units for steady 120 concurrency, with autoscale to ~10 GPUs for short bursts. If you want on-prem private we can provide a reference architecture; on-prem tends to need slightly more headroom due to less aggressive kernel tuning compared to our hosted runtime unless we ship our optimized runtime.
[00:04:40] Maya: And for quantization? We need to preserve answer quality. We can't accept hallucination increases.
[00:04:47] Samir: Right, we have quantization profiles per model that trade 8-bit/4-bit performance vs small drops in accuracy. We recommend running metric-driven evals — Redwood Optimize can run evals against your prompt set to compare quality delta. For strict quality, keep FP16 on critical routes and use int8 for non-sensitive, high-throughput endpoints.

[00:05:30] Laura: Priya — on audits, is a VPC-deployed private control plane acceptable, or do you need full air-gapped on-prem?
[00:05:38] Priya: VPC with KMS/HSM integration is likely fine. We just need firm answers on audit logs and SAML/SSO.
[00:05:45] Laura: We'll share SOC2 and our private deployment checklist after. Link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (note: placeholder)

[00:06:10] Maya: Walk me through how you do fallbacks. If Dedicated is saturated during a burst, will requests divert to Hosted? What about data egress?
[00:06:22] Samir: We can configure routing policies. For Dedicated customers we offer configurable fallbacks to a compatible model variant in Hosted in emergencies, but that's an opt-in thing due to data separation. For strict isolation, we can configure cross-region dedicated capacity or buffer queues. We'll map fallbacks to model variants with similar logits to avoid regression.
[00:07:05] Ethan: We care about token/sec numbers. In our rough calc, we need ~6,000 tokens/sec sustained during peak phases across the cluster. How does that translate to GPU count?
[00:07:18] Samir: That depends on model size, quantization, and effective batching. As a ballpark: an A100 node can often do 800-1,200 tokens/sec for mid-size models under optimized kernel paths on continuous streaming workloads. So 6,000 tokens/sec could be 6-8 GPUs with good batching. But if you enable KV caching and many cache hits, token/sec requirement for GPUs drops.
[00:07:45] Ethan: Ok. Can Redwood run a token/sec benchmark with our exact prompts? We want to know tail behavior (p95/p99).
[00:07:52] Samir: Absolutely. We usually run a 24h run to capture diurnal effects and cold starts. We'll want sample payloads, sequence length distribution, and concurrency profile. We can simulate websocket streaming to measure effective first-token latency and steady-state token/sec.

[00:08:40] Priya: Network latency matters too. Our customers are global; we'd prefer regional failover. Does Redwood do multi-region Dedicated pools?
[00:08:50] Samir: Yes, Dedicated can be geo-separated. Routing supports policy-based region selection and automatic failover. For Private on-prem, you'd be responsible for cross-region replication if you need that.

[00:09:30] Maya: Pricing question — Dedicated committed vs Hosted pay-as-you-go. We're balancing cost vs latency guarantees. Any back-of-envelope TCO?
[00:09:40] Laura: We'll send a simple TCO comparing the two. Quick note: Dedicated gives predictable unit cost and SLA; Hosted is cheaper to start but can have higher unit costs at scale. Also consider Optimize features — caching and batching often pay back quickly.

[00:10:05] Ethan: One more technical: session affinity. Our app pins sessions so KV caches help a lot. How sticky is Redwood's session pinning?
[00:10:15] Samir: We support session affinity with cookie or token-based affinity and KV cache pinning to reduce KV misses. With affinity your cache hit rate may go from, say, 30% to 70% depending on traffic patterns. That greatly improves p95.

[00:11:00] Maya: Are there any gotchas for websocket streaming? We saw jitter in prior vendors where token bursts were uneven and caused p95 spikes.
[00:11:10] Samir: Two things — network jitter and scheduling on the GPU runtime. We mitigate via per-connection priority lanes and proactive batching thresholds. We also recommend client-side rate shaping to smooth microbursts. We'll capture everything in the benchmark logs.

[00:12:00] Priya: Security: SAML, SCIM, RBAC, audit retention. Can you confirm lengths of audit logs?
[00:12:08] Laura: We can provide configurable retention; for enterprise tiers we offer 12-24 months of audit logs, plus export hooks. We'll include that in the security pack.

[00:13:10] Ethan: For the bench run, what does Redwood need from us?
[00:13:20] Samir: Ideally: 1) sample prompt set with sequence length distribution, 2) websocket traffic profile (concurrency timeline), 3) a few representative prompt templates that exercise context windows, 4) target models you want evaluated. Priya, can you share the traffic profile?
[00:13:38] Priya: Yes, we'll export a 7-day histogram and a sample of 10k requests by Friday.

[00:14:10] Maya: What about legal and procurement? We need standard enterprise terms if we go Dedicated.
[00:14:18] Laura: Our Sales Ops will send standard MSAs and a Dedicated order form; procurement tends to take 2-6 weeks depending on company. We'll flag any specific compliance clauses up front.

[00:14:50] Samir: One more practical note — if you want very low first-token p95 for short responses, prefer smaller model variants or trimmed context windows for those endpoints. That reduces KV and attention overhead.
[00:15:05] Ethan: Makes sense. We might route short-chat to a trimmed model and long summarization to the larger model. How does Redwood handle model routing?
[00:15:13] Samir: We have smart routing policies — can route by latency requirement, cost tier, or content. You can also do canary rollouts and automatic fallback in case of regression.

[00:16:00] Laura: Alright, high level recap so we can put concrete next steps on calendar. Samir will run the bench once we get payloads; Laura will send pricing and security docs; Priya will share sample traffic.
[00:16:14] Maya: Sounds good. Any blockers from your side?
[00:16:18] Priya: For VPC deployment, we need the private plane description (sic) and a KMS integration doc.
[00:16:25] Laura: We'll include both in the security pack.

[00:17:00] Ethan: One more micro detail — do you support token-level cost breakdowns per route? That helps our finance team.
[00:17:08] Laura: Yes, Console has per-route token breakdowns and cost allocation. We'll attach a screenshot example.

[00:18:00] (brief pause, side chatter)
[00:20:00] Samir: We'll tentatively schedule the bench kickoff for next week pending payloads.

[00:20:30] Maya: Good. If the bench looks good, we'll move to a 4-week pilot on Dedicated with an option to expand.

[00:21:00] Laura: Ok everyone — we'll follow up with the pack and timeline. Thanks all.
[00:21:10] (call wraps, small crosstalk)

Notes about transcription: a few proper nouns may be mis-identified (Redwood Dedicated sometimes transcribed as Redwood Dedical), and KV cache sometimes as KV cash.

References shared: Redwood security pack (link), Dedicated vs Hosted TCO spreadsheet (link), benchmark playbook (link).

End of transcript.
